_about: Batch B9 (Operating vLLM): concepts/tuning, concepts/metrics-and-observability, concepts/benchmarking, concepts/deployment-recipes, concepts/troubleshooting. Owner: the B9 writer.

max-concurrency.short: The start-up log value: KV blocks divided by the blocks that one request of max_model_len needs. It tells how many full-length requests fit in the KV cache at once.
max-concurrency.long: Computed in get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config ({{cite vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1015-1047}}) and logged as "Maximum concurrency for N tokens per request: X.XXx" ({{cite vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1090-1108}}).

performance-mode.short: A vllm serve flag with the values balanced (default), interactivity and throughput. Throughput doubles the default token budget and max_num_seqs; interactivity captures CUDA graphs for every batch size from 1 to 32.
performance-mode.long: Field {{cite vllm/config/vllm.py:440-445}}; throughput {{cite vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:3171-3175}}; interactivity {{cite vllm/config/vllm.py:2552-2556}}.

kv-cache-memory-bytes.short: A fixed KV cache size per GPU, in bytes (1G = 1 GiB). With it, the worker still runs the profile run, but skips the memory measurement and ignores --gpu-memory-utilization.
kv-cache-memory-bytes.long: Field {{cite vllm/config/cache.py:371-378}}; worker path {{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:653-679}}. The start-up log suggests a value but names it --kv-cache-memory ({{cite vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:1046-1053}}).

request-rate.short: In vllm bench serve, the mean number of requests that the client starts per second (--request-rate). The default inf sends all requests at time 0.

burstiness.short: The shape factor of the gamma distribution that vllm bench serve draws request gaps from. 1 gives a Poisson process; below 1 gives bursts; above 1 gives more even gaps.
burstiness.long: Flag {{cite vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:1754-1765}}; gamma(shape=burstiness, scale=1/(rate × burstiness)) {{cite vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:504-508}}.

goodput-slo.short: The vllm bench serve flag that sets SLOs as KEY:VALUE in milliseconds (ttft, tpot, e2el). A request is good when it meets every given SLO.

external-lb.short: A deployment where a router outside vLLM spreads requests over several vllm serve endpoints. For dense models these are independent servers; the --data-parallel-* external flags are for MoE models only.
external-lb.long: Dense models raise ValueError with external DP flags ({{cite vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:2445-2454}}).

readiness-probe.short: A periodic health request from an orchestrator (for example Kubernetes) that decides when a server gets traffic. For vllm serve it is usually GET /health.
readiness-probe.long: /health answers 200, or 503 after EngineDeadError ({{cite vllm/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/health.py:22-33}}). The vLLM docs use /health for both probes ({{cite docs/deployment/k8s.md:244-254}}).

engine-death.short: The state after the engine core process fails during serving. The front end raises EngineDeadError, requests get HTTP 500, /health answers 503 and the API server exits unless VLLM_KEEP_ALIVE_ON_ENGINE_DEATH=1.

preemption-rate.short: Preemptions per second: rate(vllm:num_preemptions_total[5m]) in PromQL. A rate above 0 means that the KV cache is too small for the running requests.
preemption-rate.long: Counter {{cite vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py:738-746}}; incremented from PREEMPTED events ({{cite vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py:580-583}}).
